title: Each cosine series term is bounded by e's own reused geometric dominant
statement: For every natural n: |(-1)^n * expTerm(2n)| <= 2 * (1/2)^n -- each cosine-series term's absolute value is dominated by CReal.e's own geometric bound, unchanged. This bounds the term's magnitude only; it discards the alternation's sign entirely, which is why the downstream numeric bounds on cosOne end up loose rather than sharp.

formal.statement: theorem CReal.cosTermAbsLeDominant : ((x0 : AxNat) -> CReal.le (CReal.abs (CReal.mul (CReal.pow (CReal.neg CReal.one) x0) (CReal.expTerm (AxNat.add x0 x0)))) (CReal.mul (CReal.ofRat (Rat.normalize (Int.ofNat (AxNat.succ (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero))) (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero) (AxNat.le.refl (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)))) (CReal.pow (CReal.ofRat (Rat.natDivSucc (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero) (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero))) x0)))
